 Order

The petitioner-accused No.2 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in SC. No.178/2022 (Crime No. 286/2022 of Tunga Nagar Police Station), registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act (for short 'D.P. Act'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Sri.Raja Naik.
2. Heard Sri.K.Ravishankar, learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri Channappa Erappa, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent -State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.
She is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
She has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
She was apprehended on 17.06.2022 and since then NC: 2023:KHC:33355 she is in judicial custody.
The investigation has been completed and the charge sheet is also filed.
The petitioner is the mother-in-law of the deceased.
First information came to be lodged for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The deceased died due to hanging.
However, allegations are made against accused Nos.1 and 2.
The complainant is already examined as PW1 but he has not fully supported the case of prosecution.
Even though PWs.2 and 3 are examined in chief, their further examination was deferred as FSL report is not yet received.
The prosecution has cited in all 44 witnesses to prove its contention.
4. Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner is a woman aged more than 60 years and is suffering from age related ailments.
Since the investigation is already completed, detention of the NC: 2023:KHC:33355 petitioner in custody would amount to pre-trial punishment.
5. Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner being woman is entitled for benefit of proviso to Section 437 of Cr.P.C.

He has placed reliance on the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this court in Nethra Vs. State of Karnataka1 and contends that even when the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC is alleged, which is punishable with death or imprisonment for life,
considering the fact that the accused is a woman, her bail application was considered by this court.
Therefore, the petitioner who is placed in similar circumstance is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Since the informant is also examined, there is no chance of influencing or tempering with the witness.

The petitioner is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the Smt. Pushpa T vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162808320/
2 petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions in Crl.P.No.2306/2022 vide order dated 12.05.2022 NC: 2023:KHC:33355 that would be imposed by this Court.

sentences.text: Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offences.

Charge sheet discloses accused Nos.1 and 2 have treated the deceased with cruelty, abused her in filthy language,
and abetted commission of suicide, by demanding for dowry.
Considering the seriousness of offence and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the accused is not entitled for grant of bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

7. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2023:KHC:33355

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 8.
The allegations made against the petitioner is of serious nature.
Similar allegations are made against both accused Nos.1 and 2 and the charge sheet is filed.
As mentioned above, 44 witnesses are cited on behalf of the prosecution.
It is stated that PW1-complainant is already examined before the trial court.
This witness has not fully supported the case of prosecution.
PW2 is the sister of the deceased.

It is stated that the deceased had sent whatsapp messages on the previous night,
describing the ill treatment meted by accused Nos.1 and 2.
These were the text messages just before the date of incident.
The said text messages sent to PW2 and 3 were said to have been sent to FSL examination.
It is stated that FSL report is not yet received.

Considering all these facts and NC:
2023:KHC:33355 circumstances, I am of the opinion that trial in the matter may take sufficiently long period of time.
9. It is stated that the petitioner is aged 60 years and suffering from age related ailment as contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
The 1st proviso to Section 437 of Cr.P.C provides for releasing the accused if she is a woman.
10. It is to be noted that petitioner had approached this court by filing Crl.P.No.9763/2022.
The said petition came to be dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 02.01.2022.
Thereafter, charge sheet is filed and prosecution witnesses are being cross examined.
It is to be noted that PWs.1 and 3 have not fully supported the case of prosecution.
11. In view of the discussions held above, detention of the petitioner in custody would amount to infringement of her right to life and liberty.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on bail subject NC: 2023:KHC:33355 to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution and its witnesses.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in SC No.178/2022 (Crime No.286/2022 of Tunga Nagar Police Station), on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
a). The petitioner shall not commit similar offences.
b). The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c).
The petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when required.
If in case, the petitioner violates any of the conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to move the Trial Court seeking cancellation of bail.

On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Trial Court is at liberty to direct the Investigating Officer to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by the petitioner and the sureties and a report may be called for in that regard, which is to be submitted by the Investigating Officer within 5 days.
The Trial Court on satisfaction, may proceed to accept the sureties for the purpose of releasing the petitioner on bail.
